candidates.name: Cerebral Autosomal Dominant Arteriopathy with Subcortical Infarcts and Leukoencephalopathy (CADASIL)
support_spans: lacunar infarctions and periventricular white matter hyperintensities (WMH)
multiple cerebral microbleeds (CMBs) and relatively fewer CMBs in deep regions, mainly involving bilateral parieto-occipital lobes
a heterozygous mutation (c.754G>A, p.A252T) in the HTRA1 gene
candidates.why: The combination of lacunar infarctions, white matter hyperintensities, cerebral microbleeds, and a family history of progressive cognitive decline and cerebral hemorrhage, along with the identified mutation in the HTRA1 gene, points towards CADASIL.

selector.runner_up: Cerebral Autosomal Dominant Arteriopathy with Subcortical Infarcts and Leukoencephalopathy (CADASIL)
selector.rationale: The presence of a heterozygous mutation in the HTRA1 gene and the clinical presentation of lacunar infarctions, periventricular white matter hyperintensities, and cerebral microbleeds support HTRA1-related cerebral small vessel disease as the most specific diagnosis.

rejected.label: Familial cerebral amyloid angiopathy
rejected.why: Lack of specific evidence for amyloid angiopathy and the presence of HTRA1 mutation points away from this diagnosis

rejected.label: HTRA1-related hereditary vasculopathy
rejected.why: While the HTRA1 mutation is present, the specific term 'cerebral small vessel disease' better explains the combination of imaging findings and genetic results
